rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding 10–20 at.% Mo to TiVNbTa to form a quinary alloy, whereas the hidden target compared CrFeTaVW with CrFeTiVW (Ta substituted by Ti) using simulations and mechanical alloying/SPS. These are different kinds of composition changes and processing routes.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions testing up to 1273 K under quasi-static loading for divertor heat-transfer conditions, while the hidden target used MD/MC simulations from 300–2100 K, SPS at 1543–1573 K, and thermal diffusivity measurements from 300–1000 K. The temperature ranges and test types (mechanical vs. thermal diffusivity) differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes Mo-induced lattice distortion, solid-solution strengthening, and a shift from screw to edge dislocation motion to improve high-temperature strength. The hidden target's mechanism involves MC-driven chemical ordering, W–W segregation, Laves-phase formation from Fe–Ta mixing enthalpy, and phonon mean free path effects on thermal diffusivity. These are entirely different mechanism classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts a 30–50% increase in yield strength at 1273 K for TiVNbTaMo. The hidden target predicted and measured similar thermal diffusivity for CrFeTaVW and CrFeTiVW, with values much lower than W and CuCrZr, and did not measure yield strength. The predicted property and direction are unrelated.
